description_full: Blackbaud, Inc. engages in the providing AI-powered solutions in the United States and internationally. The company offers fundraising and engagement solutions, including Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT, Blackbaud CRM, Blackbaud Luminate Online, Blackbaud TeamRaiser, JustGiving from Blackbaud, Blackbaud Fundraiser Performance Management, and Blackbaud Altru; financial management solutions, such as Blackbaud Financial Edge NXT, Blackbaud Purchase Cards, Blackbaud Tuition Management, Blackbaud Financial Aid Management, and Blackbaud Billing Management; and grant and award management solutions, which includes Blackbaud Grantmaking and Blackbaud Award Management. It also offers education solutions, including Blackbaud Student Information System, Blackbaud Learning Management System, Blackbaud Enrollment Management System, and Blackbaud School Website System; social responsibility, employee giving, and volunteering solutions, such as YourCause GrantsConnect and YourCause CSRconnect, and Blackbaud Impact Edge; and payment services, which includes Blackbaud Merchant Services. In addition, the company provides data intelligence solutions; professional and managed services, such as system implementation, data conversion, business process analysis and application customization, database merging and enrichment, database production activities, website design services, and outcome-based and prescriptive services; and training solutions. The company sells its solutions and related services through its direct sales force. Blackbaud, Inc. was founded in 1981 and is headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $403K ranks in the above the sector median among Technology peers, improving at 9%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $92K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $33K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (3/10).
financial_summary: Blackbaud, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.4B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $258M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.31× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 8.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 10pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.72x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+18.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 24% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 20% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 17% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 49% and a beta of 0.86, it moves roughly with the market.
About $18.6M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 51% in the 2020 crash, 44% in the 2022 bear market and 66% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 38% below its DCF fair value of $87.71, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 55%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $64.13 to $124 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 16.7 vs 26.7 and P/FCF 9.4 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 78% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 10.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $56.25 on average, 4% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 1% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.82).
It runs a 54% gross margin and converts 23% of revenue into free cash flow, or 15% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.31x.
ROE of 135% is amplified by 28.1x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 12.2% of revenue on R&D and 8.2% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.9x net debt to EBITDA ($38.9M of cash against $1.1B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.8x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.25 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.79 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 44% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.2% over 3 years and 4.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 16%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 16.9% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a backlog worth 91% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 3%.
Capex runs only 0.1x depreciation (0.7% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 19, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.0%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (11 sales, net $3.7M sold).
It returns 8.9% a year to shareholders (8.9% in buybacks).
Short interest is elevated at 11.7% of the float, 7.3 days to cover.
people: With about 2,800 employees, each generates about $403K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 8.6% a year.
That works out to $92K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $816K (2x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
